paper_title: Thinking Slow, Fast Scaling Inference Compute with Distilled Reasoners
caption: : Majority voting.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between the number of completions and majority voting accuracy. The x-axis is labeled “Number of completions (k)” and uses a logarithmic scale with values ranging from 2<sup>0</sup> to 2<sup>8</sup>, with tick labels at powers of 2. The y-axis is labeled “Majority voting accuracy” and uses a linear scale ranging from 0.3 to 0.6, with tick labels spaced at intervals of 0.1. There are three lines displayed on the plot. The first, colored teal, uses a circular marker and a solid line, starting at approximately 0.41 when k = 2<sup>0</sup> and ending at approximately 0.63 when k = 2<sup>8</sup>; this line generally increases with a steeper slope in the lower values of k, before flattening out. The second line, colored blue, features a square marker and a solid line, beginning at approximately 0.43 when k = 2<sup>0</sup> and finishing at approximately 0.64 when k = 2<sup>8</sup>; it displays a similar trend, initially increasing and then leveling off. The third line, colored light blue, uses a diamond marker and a solid line beginning at approximately 0.42 when k = 2<sup>0</sup> and ending at approximately 0.44 when k = 2<sup>8</sup>; this line shows a subtle increase across the x-axis.
